section_summary: This section follows violence and intimidation within the Japanese community in São Paulo after Japan’s surrender, especially the activities attributed to Shindo Remmei. Consular telegrams and reports describe Brazilian officials’ response, requests for Japanese newspapers and occupation films, and proposals to repatriate alleged ringleaders. Attached Brazilian press clippings debate the government’s handling of the crisis and Japanese immigration policy.

subfiles.title: Japanese community meeting and Shindo Remmei, newspaper clipping fragment
subfiles.about: Speakers urge Japanese residents to reject false claims of Japan’s victory and repudiate Shindo Remmei.
subfiles.summary: The clipping continues a meeting report and records a collective pledge to oppose Shindo Remmei.

subfiles.title: Telegram 229: murders and information campaign
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The consul reports further murders and asks for Japanese newspapers and occupation films.
subfiles.summary: Cross reports further killings, describes plans to show Japanese residents films and newspapers, and urges film shipments.

subfiles.title: Telegram 231: Japanese meeting with the interventor
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross reports that Japanese attendees challenged statements that Japan had been defeated.
subfiles.summary: He describes demands to curb press reports, revisions to a meeting record, arrests, and police concern about the consequences.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department sends Japanese newspapers for distribution in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Lists an enclosure of 22 Japanese newspaper copies.

subfiles.title: Request for a Japanese occupation film
subfiles.about: Edwards requests a 16 mm film and script for use against false victory propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Requests an extended loan of a film and script for the São Paulo Japanese community.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese newspapers
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The consulate acknowledges newspapers supplied to demonstrate Japan’s defeat.
subfiles.summary: Cross says 21 copies were forwarded to a São Paulo government official and thanks the Department.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting occupation materials
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department responds to requests for Japanese occupation materials.
subfiles.summary: A damaged instruction refers to attached materials concerning the occupation of Japan.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding Brazilian editorials
subfiles.from: American diplomatic mission, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The mission forwards editorials criticizing São Paulo’s treatment of Japanese extremists.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch encloses editorials calling for stronger measures, including trials and expulsion.

subfiles.title: Brazilian editorials on Japanese extremists
subfiles.about: Editorials criticize the Campos Elíseos meeting and demand stronger action against Shindo Remmei.
subfiles.summary: The clippings attack perceived official leniency, portray Shindo Remmei as a danger, and argue for prosecution, deportation, and restrictions on Japanese immigration.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing six packages of Japanese papers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department supplies Japanese vernacular newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Transmits six packages of newspapers, mostly from smaller Japanese towns.

subfiles.title: Instruction on materials countering Japanese propaganda
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department promises material to counter claims that Japan won the war.
subfiles.summary: Damaged instruction refers to materials for the consulate’s campaign against false victory propaganda.

subfiles.title: Telegram 243: continuing violence
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross reports murders and assaults on Brazilian officials and renews requests for information materials.
subfiles.summary: The security secretary asks about personal mail from Japan; Cross again urges films, newspapers, and a sound-truck driver.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1377: Swedish minister’s request for Japanese-language films
subfiles.about: The Swedish minister seeks convincing Japanese-language evidence of Japan’s defeat and occupation.
subfiles.summary: Pawley requests films, newsreels, and radio material for São Paulo’s Japanese population. He also reports Brazilian concern over murders and discussion of repatriating dangerous agitators.

subfiles.title: Instruction listing 17 packages of Japanese papers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department transmits regional Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Lists 17 packages of vernacular newspapers for São Paulo.

subfiles.title: Telegram 253: anti-Japanese riot in Osvaldo Cruz
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross reports a riot after a Brazilian was killed and says the sound truck has departed.
subfiles.summary: The army occupied Osvaldo Cruz after rioting; Cross still urgently requests more occupation films and a driver.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for despatch 432
subfiles.about: A routing slip circulates despatch 432.
subfiles.summary: Records internal distribution of the Rio despatch.

subfiles.title: Despatch 432: Brazilian press on Japanese colonists
subfiles.from: W. A. Wieland, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The despatch summarizes sharply divided Brazilian press reaction to São Paulo’s Japanese crisis.
subfiles.summary: Wieland surveys criticism of the interventor, Japanese immigration, police policy, and possible mass repatriation. He also records the Swedish minister’s denial that Japanese attendees behaved disrespectfully at the government-palace meeting.

subfiles.title: Interview with Swedish minister Ragnar Kumlin
subfiles.about: Kumlin defends the São Paulo meeting and denies reports of Japanese protest.
subfiles.summary: He says attendees listened respectfully and argues that persuasion of the Japanese community will take time.

subfiles.title: Editorial clippings on colonization and terrorism
subfiles.about: Editorials debate Shindo Remmei violence and the history of Japanese immigration to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: One editorial urges police action against terrorists while distinguishing them from other Japanese residents. Another calls Japanese colonization an incurable problem and argues that earlier immigration restrictions were weakened.

subfiles.title: Testemunhos da verdade sôbre os japoneses
subfiles.about: The article defends Macedo Soares’s meeting with Japanese community representatives.
subfiles.summary: It cites the meeting record and prominent Brazilian attendees to reject claims that the interventor surrendered his authority.

subfiles.title: Editorial clippings on extremists and immigration policy
subfiles.about: Editorials demand punishment of violent extremists and renewed limits on Japanese immigration.
subfiles.summary: The clippings argue over prosecution, deportation, and the long-term consequences of concentrating Japanese settlement in São Paulo.

subfiles.title: Caso dos japoneses
subfiles.about: The article assesses Macedo Soares’s policy and the arming of Japanese residents.
subfiles.summary: It supports persuasion but questions police permits to carry weapons and suggests federal intervention if state policing fails.

subfiles.title: Shindo Remmei and guerrillas, editorial clippings
subfiles.about: Editorials depict Shindo Remmei as an espionage threat and oppose civilian guerrillas.
subfiles.summary: One clipping alleges Japanese military mapping and organized influence over settlers. Another argues that regular police and federal forces should pursue suspected killers instead of armed civilian groups.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing 40 Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department sends more Japanese vernacular newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a package containing 40 newspaper copies.

subfiles.title: Telegram 256: unrest, police limits, and mob violence
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross assesses the authorities’ response as murders continue and public disorder spreads.
subfiles.summary: Cross criticizes the interventor’s meeting, says police lack the numbers for broad control, and expects eventual army intervention. He reports continuing murders, riots, looting, and concern that deported suspects might be celebrated in Japan.

subfiles.title: Telegram 260: fighting at Braúna
subfiles.from: Cecil I. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross reports fighting at Braúna despite the failure of broader predicted outbreaks.
subfiles.summary: A preliminary report describes several deaths and many injuries in the Araçatuba district.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice
subfiles.about: A form indicates that an item was removed from the file because access is restricted.
subfiles.summary: Blank identification fields leave the withdrawn item unspecified.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Jack Neal on Japanese unrest in Brazil
subfiles.about: An official forwards a confidential report on Japanese disturbances in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: The cover memorandum highlights reported assassination attempts, the failed government-palace meeting, and police difficulties.

subfiles.title: Summary of current Japanese situation in São Paulo, Brazil
subfiles.about: The report describes police investigations, proposed expulsions, attempted killings, and the July 19 meeting.
subfiles.summary: The source says police identified Japanese secret-society leaders and sought to expel 80 suspected ringleaders. It describes renewed attacks after their internment, the Japanese attendees’ rejection of surrender language at the government-palace meeting, and police resentment of the interventor’s approach. It also notes distrust of U.S. publications and continuing disagreement over how to handle the murders.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing 16 packages of Japanese papers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department forwards regional Japanese newspapers concerning occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lists 16 packages of newspapers from Japanese towns and regions.

subfiles.title: Department of State routing slip
subfiles.about: A routing slip separates records in the file.
subfiles.summary: Only the routing-slip heading is visible.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing 15 Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: American consular officer in charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department sends another selection of Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Transmits one package containing 15 newspaper copies.
